title: A2 consolidation
objectives: I can tell a short story that mixes the preterite, the imperfect and the progressive, linked with connectors.
I can use connectors such as mas, porém, então, por isso, porque, quando and enquanto, and recognize embora.
I can solve everyday problems in shops and services by complaining, exchanging, cancelling and rescheduling politely.
I can write a short informal message and a short formal email with a clear greeting, purpose, request and closing.

vocabulary.note: More formal than mas; it can also come after the first word of the clause.

example.pt: O hotel é bonito, porém muito caro.
example.en: The hotel is beautiful, but very expensive.

example.pt: Estudei muito. No entanto, não passei na prova.
example.en: I studied a lot. However, I did not pass the test.

example.pt: O apartamento é barato. Além disso, fica perto do metrô.

example.pt: Choveu muito, por isso ficamos em casa.

vocabulary.note: Formal; in speech people usually say então or por isso.

example.pt: Cheguei atrasado por causa do trânsito.

vocabulary.note: Followed by the subjunctive. For now learn the common set phrases embora seja and embora esteja.

dialogues.title: Exchanging a defective product
dialogues.context: Felipe returns to a store with headphones that stopped working. The attendant, Simone, helps him.

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Boa tarde! Em que posso ajudar?
lines.en: Good afternoon! How can I help?

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Boa tarde. Comprei este fone aqui na semana passada, mas ele está com defeito.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I bought these headphones here last week, but they are defective.

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Puxa, sinto muito. Qual é o problema?
lines.en: Oh, I am very sorry. What is the problem?

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: O som do lado direito não funciona. Eu estava ouvindo música quando ele parou de funcionar.
lines.en: The sound on the right side does not work. I was listening to music when it stopped working.

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Entendi. Você trouxe a nota fiscal?
lines.en: I see. Did you bring the receipt?

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Trouxe, está aqui. Eu queria trocar por um novo, por favor.
lines.en: I did, here it is. I would like to exchange it for a new one, please.

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Claro. A garantia vale por um ano, então não tem problema. Só preciso de um minuto para resolver isso.
lines.en: Of course. The warranty is valid for a year, so there is no problem. I just need a minute to sort this out.

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Tudo bem. Dá pra trocar por um modelo melhor?
lines.en: Fine. Can I exchange it for a better model?

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Dá, mas o modelo melhor é mais caro. Você teria que pagar a diferença.
lines.en: You can, but the better model is more expensive. You would have to pay the difference.

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Então prefiro o mesmo modelo. Embora o outro seja melhor, o preço é alto demais.
lines.en: Then I prefer the same model. Although the other one is better, the price is too high.

lines.speaker: Simone
lines.pt: Sem problema. Preencha este formulário e assine aqui, por favor.
lines.en: No problem. Fill out this form and sign here, please.

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Pronto. Muito obrigado pela ajuda!
lines.en: Done. Thank you very much for your help!

dialogues.title: The worst day of the week
dialogues.context: Daniel notices that his friend Marina looks upset and asks what happened.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Marina, você está com uma cara péssima. O que aconteceu?
lines.en: Marina, you look terrible. What happened?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Nem me fale! Ontem foi o pior dia da semana.
lines.en: Don't even ask! Yesterday was the worst day of the week.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Por quê? Me conta tudo.
lines.en: Why? Tell me everything.

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Eu estava indo para a reunião quando o ônibus quebrou no meio da avenida.
lines.en: I was going to the meeting when the bus broke down in the middle of the avenue.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Nossa! E o que você fez?
lines.en: Wow! And what did you do?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Esperei quinze minutos, mas o motorista não resolveu o problema. Então peguei um táxi.
lines.en: I waited fifteen minutes, but the driver did not fix the problem. So I took a taxi.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Chegou a tempo?
lines.en: Did you arrive on time?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Não. Enquanto eu estava no táxi, meu chefe me ligou duas vezes. Cheguei atrasada e ele ficou bravo.
lines.en: No. While I was in the taxi, my boss called me twice. I arrived late and he got angry.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Mas você explicou o que aconteceu?
lines.en: But did you explain what happened?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Expliquei, porém ele não acreditou. Por isso hoje eu saí mais cedo de casa.
lines.en: I did, but he did not believe me. That is why I left home earlier today.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.pt: Bem pensado. Se eu fosse você, eu mandaria uma mensagem para ele agora, pedindo desculpas.
lines.en: Good thinking. If I were you, I would send him a message now, apologizing.

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Vou te mandar o texto antes para você ver.
lines.en: Good idea. I will send you the text first so you can see it.

dialogues.title: Rescheduling a dinner
dialogues.context: Rita tells her friends Pedro and Clara that their restaurant reservation was cancelled. They decide what to do.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Pessoal, tenho um problema. O restaurante cancelou a nossa reserva de sábado.
lines.en: Guys, I have a problem. The restaurant cancelled our Saturday reservation.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Sério? Por quê?
lines.en: Really? Why?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Por causa de um problema na cozinha. Mas eles me ofereceram outro horário.
lines.en: Because of a problem in the kitchen. But they offered me another time.

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Dá pra remarcar para domingo? Embora seja em cima da hora, eu prefiro domingo.
lines.en: Can we reschedule for Sunday? Although it is last minute, I prefer Sunday.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Domingo é melhor para mim também. Além disso, o restaurante fica mais vazio.
lines.en: Sunday is better for me too. Besides, the restaurant is emptier.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Boa! Vou ligar agora e remarcar a reserva. Que horas vocês preferem?
lines.en: Great! I will call now and reschedule the reservation. What time do you prefer?

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Às oito seria ótimo. Antes disso eu tenho um compromisso.
lines.en: Eight would be great. Before that I have an engagement.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Pra mim pode ser. Mas não se esqueça de confirmar o número de pessoas.
lines.en: That works for me. But do not forget to confirm the number of people.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.pt: Pode deixar. Enquanto eu ligo, vocês avisam o resto do grupo?
lines.en: Leave it to me. While I call, will you let the rest of the group know?

lines.speaker: Clara
lines.pt: Aviso, sim. Vou mandar uma mensagem agora.
lines.en: I will. I am going to send a message now.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: E eu mando um áudio. Daqui a pouco todo mundo fica sabendo.
lines.en: And I will send a voice message. In a little while everybody will know.

grammar.title: Connectors: linking ideas
grammar.explanation:
Connectors turn short sentences into a story. Mas is the everyday word for but; porém and no entanto are more formal and common in writing. Então and por isso introduce a result (so, that is why), and porque introduces a reason (because). For a reason followed by a noun, use por causa de: por causa da chuva. Quando links events in time, and enquanto links two actions that happen at the same time: Enquanto eu cozinhava, ele lia.

Embora means although. It takes the subjunctive, which you will learn later, so at this stage simply recognize and reuse the common phrases embora seja and embora esteja: Embora seja caro, vale a pena. Além disso adds a point, ou seja clarifies, and mesmo assim means even so.

Do not confuse the four spellings of why and because. Por que (two words) starts a question: Por que você saiu? Porque (one word) gives an answer: Porque estava cansado. Por quê (with the accent) comes at the end of a question: Você saiu por quê? And o porquê is the noun the reason: Não sei o porquê.

grammar.title: Review: telling a story and the A2 toolkit
grammar.explanation:
A story in Portuguese usually has three parts: the setting, the trigger and the result. The setting uses the imperfect to describe background and ongoing situations: Eram oito horas, chovia, eu estava indo para o trabalho. The trigger is a sudden event in the preterite: de repente, o ônibus quebrou. The result is one or more preterite actions: liguei para o chefe, peguei um táxi.

The pattern estava plus gerund with quando plus preterite is the classic pair: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou. Enquanto joins two ongoing actions in the imperfect: Enquanto eu cozinhava, ele arrumava a casa. For what is happening now, use estar plus gerund in the present.

To finish a story, combine the other A2 tools: comparatives for opinions (foi o pior dia da semana), object pronouns placed before the verb (ele me ligou), imperatives for advice (mande uma mensagem), and ir plus infinitive or the simple future for what comes next (vou pedir desculpas).

grammar.title: Common A2 errors
grammar.explanation:
Most mistakes at this level come from four areas. First, the past tenses: use the imperfect for habits and background (Quando eu era criança, eu ia à praia) and the preterite for a sudden or completed event (De repente, o telefone tocou). Second, irregular preterites: say fiz, trouxe, soube and disse, never fazi, trazi, sabi or dizi.

Third, pronouns: when the pronoun is the subject of an infinitive, use eu, not mim (É difícil para eu entender), and place weak pronouns before the verb in speech (Ele me ligou, not Ele ligou-me). Fourth, gender and number: nouns ending in -ma such as problema, sistema, programa and tema are masculine, while a mão and a foto are feminine despite the -o. Plurals of nouns in -ão vary (mãos, pães, limões), and -l changes to -is (animal, animais).

Finally, remember that Portuguese expresses many states with estar com or ter rather than ser: Estou com fome, Tenho vinte anos, Estou com frio. And in Brazil the progressive is estou trabalhando, never estou a trabalhar.

grammar.title: Writing short messages and emails
grammar.explanation:
A good short message has four parts: a greeting, a reason for writing, a request or piece of information, and a closing. For a friend, keep it short and warm: Oi, Ana! Tudo bem? Estou escrevendo para avisar que vou atrasar. Me manda a localização? Um abraço! In messaging apps, abbreviations such as vc, pq and tb are common among friends, but avoid them at work.

For a formal email, open with Prezado or Prezada plus the person's title and name, or just Bom dia. State the purpose clearly with Estou escrevendo para, make one request per paragraph with Você poderia or Gostaria de, mention attachments with Segue em anexo, and close with Agradeço desde já and Atenciosamente followed by your name. Aguardo o seu retorno is a polite way to ask for a reply.

Use short sentences, connectors such as mas, além disso and por isso to link ideas, and a date or deadline when you need an answer. Reread the message before sending it, especially for accents and for the forms of você and o senhor.

culture.title: Complaints, consumer rights and tone
culture.text:
Brazilians usually begin a complaint politely. Even on the phone with a bad problem, people start with Boa tarde, tudo bem? and explain calmly before asking for a solution. In stores, the key documents are the nota fiscal and the garantia. Consumer protection in Brazil is strong on paper: the Código de Defesa do Consumidor, and the agency Procon, help customers who have problems with products and services. For purchases made online or by phone, the law gives the customer seven days to change their mind and get a refund.

Most companies run a customer service line called SAC, Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor, and many customers also post public complaints on websites and social media, where a quick reply from the company is common. In writing, the tone changes with the reader: Oi, tudo bem? for a friend, and Prezado senhor or Prezada senhora plus Atenciosamente for a company or a boss. A message to a friend might end with Um abraço or Beijos, while an email to a company ends with Atenciosamente and your full name.

paragraphs.pt: Prezados, bom dia. Estou escrevendo para fazer uma reclamação sobre um pedido.
paragraphs.en: Dear sirs, good morning. I am writing to make a complaint about an order.

paragraphs.pt: Na semana passada, comprei um fone de ouvido no site de vocês. Quando a encomenda chegou, o fone estava quebrado.
paragraphs.en: Last week, I bought a pair of headphones on your website. When the order arrived, the headphones were broken.

paragraphs.pt: Liguei para o atendimento, mas ninguém me respondeu. Enquanto eu esperava na linha, a ligação caiu. Por isso, estou escrevendo.
paragraphs.en: I called customer service, but nobody answered me. While I was waiting on the line, the call dropped. That is why I am writing.

paragraphs.pt: Gostaria de trocar o produto por um novo. Também gostaria de saber se posso cancelar a compra e receber o reembolso. Segue em anexo a nota fiscal.
paragraphs.en: I would like to exchange the product for a new one. I would also like to know whether I can cancel the purchase and receive a refund. The receipt is attached.

paragraphs.pt: Agradeço desde já e aguardo o retorno de vocês. Atenciosamente, Lucas Ferreira.
paragraphs.en: Thank you in advance, and I look forward to your reply. Sincerely, Lucas Ferreira.
